item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01775","case1_error":"Counts only two houses instead of Zion's house plus his two friends' houses.","case2_error":"Counts two small gates plus one large gate, although only one of each is specified.","reason":"Both use incorrect item multiplicities when aggregating the specified objects; their subsequent arithmetic follows those incorrect counts.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J01776","case1_error":"Gives an unsupported final value of 200 after correctly stating the formula for the value increase, which yields $600.","case2_error":"Applies the doubling of fuel capacity twice, turning the correct $480 total into $960.","reason":"The first supplies an incorrect number after correct formulas without showing its calculation; the second explicitly duplicates a capacity multiplier.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01777","case1_error":"Models five children and five adults instead of three children and two adults.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates the correctly written sum 5 + 20 + 18 as 41 instead of 43.","reason":"The first sets up an erroneous ticket-count equation; the second makes a numerical evaluation error in a correct expression.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01778","case1_error":"Multiplies the required length by 0.75, reducing the purchase requirement instead of compensating for rope lost.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates $14 divided by the price of $2 per three pieces as two pieces; it buys 21 pieces.","reason":"The first uses an erroneous relation for compensating loss; the second incorrectly evaluates the stated money-to-quantity division.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01779","case1_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 30 + 35 + 46 as 101 instead of 111.","case2_error":"Uses 100 − 30 + 10 for the new female count instead of 30 + 10.","reason":"The first miscalculates a correctly written sum; the second writes an incorrect relation for the population being counted.","judgment":"different"}]}
